phase.name: Organization, Geography & Configuration
phase.objective: Establish the organization, branch, geographic, financial-year, numbering, application-setting, printer, and barcode configuration capabilities required by the Pharmacy ERP.
phase.objective_context: This phase builds the configuration and reference foundation that later business modules depend on.

scope.out_of_scope_note: Those capabilities are covered in later phases.

epic.title: Organization, Geography & Configuration
epic.description: Provide the core organization and configuration capabilities required for the Pharmacy ERP to operate consistently across companies, branches, financial years, geographic locations, document sequences, application settings, printers, and barcode functionality.
epic.technical_context: The database overview identifies Company, Branch, FinancialYear, SequenceGenerator, AppSetting, PrinterConfiguration, and BarcodeConfiguration as configuration tables, while Country, State, City, and Area form the geographic master hierarchy.
epic.business_value: These capabilities provide the reference context required by later ERP transactions. Purchase, sales, inventory, party addresses, financial processing, printing, and document numbering should depend on standardized configuration rather than hardcoded values.
completion_criteria: Tests cover core and negative scenarios.

user_stories.title: Create company
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to create a company so that the ERP has a defined organization context.
acceptance_criteria: An authorized user can create a company.
Mandatory company information is validated.
Duplicate company information is rejected according to defined uniqueness rules.
A new company receives the standard system identifiers and audit fields.
The company can subsequently be associated with branches.
Invalid requests return standardized validation errors.

tasks.title: Add Company authorization
details: Restrict company configuration to appropriate administrative permissions.

user_stories.title: View and search companies
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can view companies.
Search/filter behavior is available where required.
Deleted companies are excluded from normal views.
Pagination is applied where the dataset requires it.

user_stories.title: Update and deactivate company
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can update permitted company information.
Invalid changes are rejected.
A company can be deactivated according to business rules.
Deactivated companies are not selectable for new transactions where applicable.
Existing historical records remain intact.

user_stories.title: Create branch
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to create a branch under a company so that the ERP can manage multiple operational locations.
acceptance_criteria: A branch belongs to a valid company.
Mandatory branch information is validated.
Branch uniqueness rules are enforced within the applicable organization scope.
A branch can reference geographic master data.
An inactive company cannot receive new operational branches unless explicitly allowed.
Branch identifiers and audit fields are generated consistently.

user_stories.title: View and search branches
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can list branches.
Branches can be filtered by company.
Branch status is visible.
Deleted branches are excluded from normal results.

user_stories.title: Update and deactivate branch
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can update branch information.
Branch deactivation is supported.
Deactivated branches cannot be selected for new operational transactions where applicable.
Historical references remain valid.

user_stories.title: Manage countries
user_stories.user_story: As an administrator, I want to maintain country master data so that addresses can use standardized geographic references.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can create countries.
Country name/code validation is applied.
Duplicate country records are prevented according to the defined uniqueness rules.
Countries can be viewed and searched.
Countries can be deactivated/soft-deleted according to dependency rules.
Countries referenced by existing records cannot be physically removed.

tasks.title: Define Country model constraints and indexes

user_stories.title: Manage states within countries
user_stories.user_story: As an administrator, I want to maintain states under countries so that the geographic hierarchy remains consistent.
acceptance_criteria: Every state belongs to one valid country.
A state cannot be created without a valid parent country.
State uniqueness is enforced within the applicable country.
Country filtering is supported.
Invalid parent references are rejected.
Existing referenced states are protected from unsafe deletion.

user_stories.title: Manage cities within states
user_stories.user_story: As an administrator, I want to maintain cities under states so that the geographic hierarchy can be used consistently by addresses and operational processes.
acceptance_criteria: Every city belongs to one valid state.
A city cannot be created without a valid parent state.
City uniqueness is enforced within the applicable state.
State selection filters available cities appropriately.
Invalid parent relationships are rejected.
Referenced cities cannot be physically removed unsafely.

user_stories.title: Manage areas within cities
user_stories.user_story: As an administrator, I want to maintain areas under cities so that the ERP can use the lowest-level geographic reference for addresses and operational processes.
acceptance_criteria: Every area belongs to one valid city.
An area cannot be created without a valid parent city.
Area code/name uniqueness follows the defined business scope.
City selection is supported.
Invalid parent relationships are rejected.
Referenced areas cannot be physically removed unsafely.

user_stories.title: Provide cascading geographic selection
user_stories.user_story: As a user entering an address, I want geographic selections to follow the Country → State → City → Area hierarchy so that invalid combinations cannot be selected.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a country limits available states.
Selecting a state limits available cities.
Selecting a city limits available areas.
Clearing a parent selection clears or invalidates dependent selections.
The backend validates the complete hierarchy rather than trusting UI selections.
Invalid geographic combinations are rejected.

tasks.title: Add geographic lookup caching where appropriate
Create shared backend geographic lookup service
Create shared frontend geographic lookup service

user_stories.title: Create financial year
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to define a financial year so that financial and operational transactions can be associated with the correct period.
acceptance_criteria: A financial year has a defined start and end.
Start date must precede end date.
Overlapping financial years are prevented according to business rules.
Financial year status is maintained.
Financial year information is auditable.

user_stories.title: Activate and close financial year
acceptance_criteria: An authorized administrator can activate a financial year.
Business rules prevent multiple invalid active periods.
Closing a financial year prevents prohibited transactions.
Historical records remain accessible.
Financial year state transitions are auditable.

user_stories.title: Resolve current financial year
acceptance_criteria: The system can determine the applicable financial year for a date.
The result is consistent across backend services.
Invalid or ambiguous periods are rejected.
Later transaction modules can consume the service.

user_stories.title: Define document numbering sequence
user_stories.user_story: As an administrator, I want to configure document sequences so that ERP transactions receive controlled business document numbers.
acceptance_criteria: A sequence can be defined for a supported document type.
Sequence configuration can include the required numbering parameters.
Duplicate sequence definitions are prevented.
Sequence status can be managed.
Sequence configuration can be associated with the appropriate organization/branch scope where applicable.

user_stories.title: Generate the next document number safely
acceptance_criteria: The system can request the next number for a configured sequence.
Numbers are generated without unintended duplication.
Concurrent requests are handled safely.
Failed transactions do not create unacceptable numbering corruption.
The sequence behavior is documented for later transaction modules.

tasks.title: Define transaction/concurrency strategy for sequence allocation

user_stories.title: Integrate sequence generation with transaction modules
user_stories.notes: This story establishes the integration contract; actual Purchase/Sales document integrations belong to their respective phases.

tasks.title: Document integration pattern for later modules

user_stories.title: Manage application settings
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to manage application settings so that configurable system behavior can be changed without modifying source code.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can view supported settings.
Authorized users can modify permitted settings.
Setting values are validated according to their type.
Unsupported setting keys cannot be created through unrestricted input.
Sensitive values are protected.
Setting changes are auditable where appropriate.

tasks.title: Define AppSetting model and configuration rules

user_stories.title: Provide application settings to runtime components

tasks.title: Implement frontend configuration lookup where required

user_stories.title: Configure printers
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to configure printers so that the ERP can use the correct printer for supported output operations.
acceptance_criteria: Printer configuration can be created.
Printer details are validated.
Printer configuration can be associated with the applicable company/branch/context where required.
A default printer can be identified according to business rules.
Inactive printers cannot be selected for new print operations.
Configuration changes are auditable where appropriate.

tasks.title: Implement printer availability/configuration check where supported

user_stories.title: Configure barcode behavior
user_stories.user_story: As an authorized administrator, I want to configure barcode behavior so that barcode-based workflows can use consistent system settings.
acceptance_criteria: Barcode configuration can be created and updated.
Supported configuration values are validated.
Configuration can be scoped appropriately.
Invalid barcode configuration is rejected.
Barcode configuration can be consumed by later inventory/sales functionality.

user_stories.title: Provide reusable barcode configuration to transaction modules

tasks.title: Document integration with later inventory/sales modules

cross_cutting.title: Cross-Cutting Authorization
cross_cutting.description: Every administrative configuration capability introduced in this phase must use the security framework from Phase 1 and later be connected to the full User/Role/Permission implementation in Phase 4.

cross_cutting.title: Cross-Cutting Audit Integration
cross_cutting.description: The complete AuditLog/ChangeHistory implementation is covered later. This phase should nevertheless identify auditable configuration changes.

tasks.title: Review Phase 2 schema for naming consistency
Review Phase 2 indexes and unique constraints

dependencies.flow_note: Phase 2 depends on Phase 1. Later business modules consume Phase 2 organization, geographic, financial-year, numbering, and configuration capabilities.

completion_checklist: Country → State → City → Area hierarchy validated.

phase_boundary.statement: Phase 2 establishes the organizational and configuration context.
phase_boundary.does_not_implement: It does not implement downstream business transactions.
examples: Phase 6: Inventory → uses Branch, Medicine, UOM, configuration
Phase 7: Purchase → uses Supplier, Medicine, Branch, FinancialYear, Sequence
Phase 8: Sales → uses Customer, Medicine, Branch, FinancialYear, Sequence
Phase 9: Financial → uses FinancialYear and transaction context
phase_boundary.boundary_note: This boundary keeps the ADO backlog dependency-driven rather than mixing unrelated business functionality into the configuration phase.
